scope: Security, privacy, compliance, and supply-chain review of the proposed local-first desktop download manager. No executable application, dependency manifest, package, signing operation, deployment, or production activity is approved or performed.

limitations: The repository contains planning records but no executable source, dependency manifest, lockfile, CI workflow, package, or runtime test surface.
The first platform, supported versions, implementation stack, persistence technology, browser integration, telemetry, update mechanism, and distribution channel are not approved.
This is a design-time threat model and control plan, not penetration-test, vulnerability-scan, privacy-audit, compliance-certification, or release-readiness evidence.

securityBoundary.businessRules: One UI-independent download domain or service owns state transitions, URL and destination policy, retry/resume decisions, cancellation, conflict handling, finalization, and recovery. UI, browser, filesystem, persistence, transfer, packaging, and test adapters consume it and may not redefine these rules.
protectedAssets: authentication headers, cookies, tokens, and proxy credentials
destination paths and local file contents
release source, binaries, checksums, provenance, SBOM, and signing identities
local diagnostics and any future consent record

trustBoundaries.boundary: untrusted remote server and redirect chain -> transfer engine
trustBoundaries.default: deny unsupported schemes and unsafe redirects; validate every hop

trustBoundaries.boundary: transfer engine -> partial and completed filesystem objects
trustBoundaries.default: write only to an application-controlled partial file; finalize atomically after validation

trustBoundaries.boundary: desktop UI or CLI adapter -> shared domain service
trustBoundaries.default: typed, versioned commands; reject stale or invalid transitions without mutation
absent until approved; authenticated, versioned, consent-bound messages if introduced

trustBoundaries.boundary: persistent metadata and diagnostics -> local users, support, or telemetry
trustBoundaries.default: local-only, least data, restrictive access, redaction, bounded retention

trustBoundaries.boundary: source and dependencies -> build and signed release artifact
trustBoundaries.default: locked inputs, isolated build/signing, provenance and independent verification

trustBoundaries.boundary: update metadata or distribution channel -> installed application
trustBoundaries.default: automatic updates absent until signed metadata, anti-rollback, ownership, and recovery are approved

threatModel.threat: SSRF or local-network access through user-supplied URLs and redirects
requiredControls: Allow only approved schemes
Canonicalize and validate the initial URL and every redirect
Define policy for loopback, link-local, private, multicast, file, and platform-specific schemes
Apply DNS-rebinding-aware address checks where private destinations are denied
Bound redirects, response headers, timeouts, and response sizes
threatModel.verification: Deterministic integration server tests cover blocked address classes, redirect-to-blocked targets, DNS changes, malformed locations, and allowed public HTTP(S) behavior.

threatModel.threat: Credential disclosure across origins, redirects, logs, clipboard, UI, or diagnostics
requiredControls: Never forward Authorization, Cookie, or proxy credentials to a different origin without an explicit approved policy
Redact URL user-info and sensitive query values
Store secrets only in approved OS credential storage if authenticated downloads enter scope
Exclude raw headers and tokens from errors and diagnostics
threatModel.verification: Cross-origin redirect and diagnostic-capture tests use canary secrets and assert no disclosure in requests, logs, UI, crash data, or persisted metadata.

threatModel.threat: Path traversal, symlink or junction abuse, unsafe overwrite, device-name handling, or write outside the selected destination
requiredControls: Treat server filenames as untrusted display suggestions
Generate safe local names and validate canonical destination containment
Reject traversal, absolute paths, reserved names, alternate streams, and embedded separators according to platform policy
Use no-follow or equivalent race-resistant file operations
Never overwrite without an approved explicit conflict decision
threatModel.verification: Platform filesystem tests cover traversal encodings, symlinks/junctions, rename races, locked files, reserved names, case collisions, removable volumes, and destination permission loss.

threatModel.threat: Silent corruption or content substitution during resume and finalization
requiredControls: Append only after a valid range response and matching remote identity
Reject overlapping, missing, malformed, compressed, or inconsistent ranges
Keep partial files distinct from completed files
Flush, close, verify approved integrity evidence, then atomically finalize and persist completed last
threatModel.verification: Integration tests cover ignored ranges, changed ETag or Last-Modified, inconsistent length, truncation, disk exhaustion, termination, restart, and finalization failure with byte-level integrity checks.

threatModel.threat: Resource exhaustion from unbounded concurrency, retry storms, oversized metadata, decompression, disk consumption, or slow peers
requiredControls: Bound global and per-origin concurrency
Use capped exponential backoff with jitter and retry budgets
Enforce header, filename, metadata, queue, memory-buffer, and disk-reserve limits
Stream content rather than buffering whole files
Make cancellation prompt and cleanup policy explicit
threatModel.verification: Adversarial workload tests measure CPU, memory, descriptors, disk, network, UI responsiveness, cancellation latency, and retry volume against approved budgets.

threatModel.threat: Browser integration grants unauthorized filesystem, process, credential, or download authority
requiredControls: Keep browser capture excluded by default
Authenticate and version native messages
Allowlist message shapes and extension identities
Require visible user consent and revocation
Expose only narrow intake commands; never arbitrary paths, process execution, headers, or direct state mutation
threatModel.verification: Browser/runtime tests cover forged origins, replay, malformed and oversized messages, downgrade, revoked consent, extension replacement, and unauthorized capability requests.

threatModel.threat: Downloaded active content is mistaken for trusted application output
requiredControls: Do not execute or auto-open downloads
Preserve operating-system quarantine or origin metadata where available
Use neutral completion messaging
Document antivirus and reputation-tool interaction
Require explicit user action to reveal or open files
threatModel.verification: Platform runtime tests confirm no execution, quarantine behavior, safe reveal/open flow, and clear warnings for executable content.

threatModel.threat: Tampered dependency, build runner, package, update, or stolen signing identity compromises users
requiredControls: Approve license and dependency policy before adding dependencies
Pin direct and transitive inputs with a lockfile and verify native binary provenance
Use least-privilege isolated builds and release-only signing
Produce checksums, SBOM, and provenance bound to the immutable artifact
Sign update metadata and artifacts, enforce freshness and anti-rollback, and document revocation and recovery
threatModel.verification: Dependency, license, vulnerability, secret, provenance, signature, tamper, rollback, and repeated-build checks run on the canonical revision and exact release artifact.

privacyReview.baseline: Local-first with remote telemetry absent by default. The application must remain functional without an account or cloud service unless a later human-approved scope explicitly requires one.

dataInventory.sensitivity: may reveal identity, interests, tokens, or local organization
dataInventory.defaultHandling: persist only fields required for recovery; redact sensitive URL components; local-only
do not persist or log; use OS credential storage only under an approved authenticated-download design
never inspect, upload, or retain beyond user-visible download and cancellation policies
local, redacted, bounded retention, explicit export
absent; any future collection requires separate specification, consent, minimization, retention, deletion, and offline controls

userControls: Clear download history without deleting completed files unless separately confirmed
Delete retained partial files according to an approved cancellation policy
Inspect and explicitly export redacted diagnostics
Revoke browser integration if later approved
Use the core application with telemetry disabled
privacyReview.retention: Retention periods and deletion behavior require human approval before implementation. Defaults must minimize history and avoid indefinite credential, sensitive URL, diagnostic, or consent-record retention.
privacyReview.researchPrivacy: Any discovery evidence must minimize participant data and document consent, access, retention, deletion, anonymization, and representation limitations; no participant data was accessed in this workstream.

openSourceReleaseBlockers: Dependency exception owner and expiry process
Contribution governance and developer certificate or CLA decision
Public vulnerability-reporting channel and safe-harbor policy
Signing-key custodian, rotation, revocation, and recovery
claimsNotMade: No claim of GDPR, CCPA, accessibility, export-control, cryptographic, store-policy, code-signing, or other legal compliance
No claim that source or binary distribution is approved
No claim that dependencies are vulnerability-free or license-compatible
No claim of secure implementation, penetration testing, privacy certification, or release readiness
complianceAndGovernance.requiredLegalReview: Applicable privacy notices, consent requirements, export controls, sanctions, platform-store terms, third-party notices, and license compatibility depend on approved features, jurisdictions, dependencies, and distribution channels and require qualified review before release.

supplyChainReview.observedState: No package.json, package-lock.json, dependency manifest, dependency lockfile, executable source tree, CI workflow, package, SBOM, provenance, or signing material was present in the inspected implementation boundary.
supplyChainReview.disposition: No dependency vulnerability or license scan can truthfully run yet. Public release remains blocked, not passed.
requiredPolicy: Minimize dependencies and document why each direct dependency is needed.
Allow only approved licenses and provenance; reject unreviewed vendored or prebuilt native binaries.
Commit the selected ecosystem lockfile and enforce immutable or frozen restore in CI.
Pin CI actions and toolchains to immutable revisions and use read-only permissions for untrusted pull requests.
Generate and retain dependency inventory, license report, vulnerability results, SBOM, provenance, and artifact checksums.
Define severity-based remediation SLAs plus attributed, expiring, documented exceptions.
Keep signing and publishing credentials out of source, pull-request jobs, ordinary CI, logs, and artifacts.
Promote the exact independently verified artifact; rebuilding invalidates prior security evidence.

securityAcceptanceGates.gate: Human product, first-platform, MVP, and data-flow decisions
Approved license, dependency rules, governance, vulnerability reporting, release ownership, and signing custody
Implemented shared domain and adapter controls with unit and contract tests
Adversarial network, filesystem, restart, browser-if-applicable, and sensitive-log integration tests
Locked dependency inventory, license and vulnerability results, secret scan, SBOM, and provenance
Platform package, signature, update-if-applicable, revocation, rollback, and clean-install runtime verification

traceability.limitation: Observable download behavior and integrity scenarios are not implemented.
Platform and architecture selections remain unapproved.
Controls are required gates, not approved governance or distribution evidence.
Browser integration, authenticated downloads, telemetry, and automatic updates remain excluded, deferred, or undecided.
Independent disposition is reserved for ENG-15.
No participant evidence was accessed or assessed.

implementationNotes: No application, dependency, CI, database, infrastructure, credential, package, signing, deployment, branch, or commit change was made.
Threats and controls are centralized around the shared domain/service boundary; adapters must not duplicate security-sensitive business rules.
No user-visible behavior exists in this workstream, so DOM, browser, integration, or equivalent runtime evidence is not applicable to this documentation-only change.
Only local, test, and staging are declared. Production and public distribution require separate attributed human approval.
knownRisks: There is no executable implementation, so every technical mitigation remains unimplemented and untested.
Product and platform decisions may materially change trust boundaries, privacy data flows, legal obligations, and the threat model.
Credentialed downloads, browser integration, automatic updates, and telemetry would each add critical attack or privacy surfaces and require separate approval and testing.

Resume and destination handling can cause silent corruption or unintended overwrite unless remote identity, range semantics, canonical paths, and atomic finalization are tested on each supported platform.
License, dependency, governance, vulnerability response, signing custody, and release ownership are unresolved blockers to open-source or binary distribution.
Independent verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
